title: Hybrid kernel fingerprint profiler + per-request recommender for arch & seqlen regimes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Kernel selection currently uses static heuristics that degrade across model architectures and sequence-length regimes. This ticket proposes a hybrid approach: a lightweight fingerprint-based profiler that classifies request regimes (model architecture signature + sequence-length distribution + hardware flavor) and a background micro-benchmarking/autotune runner that produces per-regime kernel recommendations. These recommendations are surfaced to the runtime's scheduler as a fast lookup with confidence scores and fallbacks, improving latency/cost tradeoffs for both prefill and decode phases.

Goals: Provide a robust, low-overhead per-request kernel recommender that: 1) Reduces median p50/p95 token latency for decode-heavy workloads; 2) Increases prefill throughput for long-context batches without raising tail latency beyond SLO; 3) Automatically adapts when new kernels/quantized builds are introduced; 4) Ships feature-flagged with A/B metrics for us to validate improvements.

Non-goals: Full online RL tuning, global retraining of heuristics, replacing the existing fallback safety net. This is an incremental autotune layer integrated with current scheduler fallback paths.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler fingerprinting latency <= 0.25 ms added per request on x86 and <= 0.35 ms on aarch64
Autotune runner produces a kernel recommendation with a confidence score for >= 90% of observed regime-model pairs within 48 hours of first seeing them in the fleet

A/B experiment shows >= 8% reduction in decode p95 token latency for targeted decode-heavy workloads and >= 12% increase in prefill throughput for batchy long-context workloads, without >2% error rate increase
Feature is behind runtime feature flag and can be turned off without restart. Rollback reverts to previous static heuristic behavior with no state loss
Unit + integration tests covering profiler mapping, cache invalidation, fallback paths, and safety limits are included
tasks: Design fingerprint schema and canonicalize model/hw signature (Aisha)
Implement lightweight request fingerprinting hook in prefill/decode paths (Riley)
Background micro-benchmark runner service that schedules per-node short kernel trials (DevOps + infra)
Create central recommendations cache with TTLs and versioning (Datastore team)
Integrate confidence-aware policy into scheduler to pick recommendation or fallback (Riley)
Build A/B experiment config and dashboards (Growth/Analytics)
Safety audit for regressions and fallback thresholds (SRE)
End-to-end tests and canary rollout plan (QA + Eng)
design_notes:
High-level approach:
1) Fingerprint: compute a compact regime key per request: model hash (canonicalized model family + param bucket), quantization tag, hw flavor, and sequence-length bucket (0-64,65-256,257-1024,1025+). Keep key <= 64 bits for fast map lookups.
2) Micro-benchmark runner: when a new regime is first observed on a node type, schedule a short, isolated micro-benchmark that runs candidate kernels across short synthetic prefill/decode tasks with representative batch sizes and token lengths. Use wall-clock token throughput and tail-latency telemetry. Each run is limited to 500 ms of runtime per candidate kernel and recorded to the central store.
3) Scoring: compute a composite score that weights decode latency tail more heavily for interactive regimes and prefill throughput more for batchy regimes. Include penalty terms for memory/regalloc pressure and observed OOMs. Normalize scores across hardware families.
4) Confidence: recommendations start at low confidence; confidence increases after repeated, consistent micro-benchmark results and live production telemetry that confirms behavior within a tolerance band.
5) Runtime integration: scheduler performs a single lock-free lookup per request using the fingerprint. If recommendation exists and confidence > threshold it applies; else fall back to existing heuristic. All picks are logged with sampling for offline analysis.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Running micro-benchmarks on production nodes increases CPU/GPU cycles; to mitigate, runs are piggybacked during low-util windows and rate-limited per node.
- Small benchmark durations may miss pathologies; we mitigate by combining micro-benchmarks with passive live telemetry validation.
- Fingerprint granularity: too coarse hides important patterns; too fine causes cold-start. We will iterate on bucket boundaries based on telemetry.

Implementation milestones:
- Week 1-2: fingerprint schema + unit tests + in-process lookup hook
- Week 3-4: micro-benchmark runner prototype + central result ingestion API
- Week 5: scoring function and confidence model + integration tests
- Week 6: internal canary across staging fleet + A/B metrics collection
- Week 7-8: extended canary to 10% production, iterate thresholds
- Week 9: rollout to all nodes behind flag, monitoring + rollback window
rollout_plan: 1) Launch behind feature flag. 2) Canary on staging cluster for 48 hours with synthetic workload. 3) Canary to 1% production nodes for 72 hours (observe error rates & latency). 4) Ramp to 10% for 7 days and evaluate KPIs. 5) If KPIs met, ramp to 50% then 100% over 2 weeks. 6) Automatic rollback if decode p95 increases beyond configured SLO breach (default +3%) or if error-rate delta > 1.5x baseline.
metrics: customer-visible error rate and latency SLO breaches
